PullRequest.Title: agentHost: preserve plugin agent invocation restrictions
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #342092, addressing [the model-invocation restriction finding](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/342092#discussion_r4296472550) and [the synced-agent selection finding](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/342092#discussion_r4296472613).

Plugin agents projected into the Copilot runtime's explicit catalog now carry `disableModelInvocation: true` when either `disable-model-invocation: true` or its deprecated `infer: false` equivalent restricts delegation. The provider integration test now selects the parent through its published, synced plugin child URI and verifies both that a normal sibling can be delegated to and that a restricted sibling cannot.

## Validation

- Passed — `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`
- Passed — `npm run typecheck-client`
- Passed — `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotPluginConverters.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotPluginConverters.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/copilotMockLlm.integrationTest.ts`
- Passed — `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotPluginConverters.test.ts` (44 tests)
- Passed — `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/copilotMockLlm.integrationTest.ts --grep 'selected plugin agent delegates'` (1 test)

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a non-ephemeral Copilot session with plugin agents
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session launch calls toSdkSessionCustomAgents while building SDK config, waits for it alongside BYOK and shell-tool setup in Promise.all, then crosses the existing SDK createSession/resumeSession boundary. The diff adds a constant-time boolean resolver and an optional field before that boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse each plugin agent Markdown file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential read per agent resource in the resolved plugin snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same loop read the same files and parsed the same frontmatter before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before SDK session creation/resumption, although it overlaps independent BYOK and shell-tool work

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the completed session configuration to the Copilot SDK runtime via createSession or resumeSession
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK session call per launch attempt; fallback paths are unchanged
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same custom-agent catalog crossed the same SDK boundary; restricted entries simply lacked one boolean field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The session cannot become usable until this existing SDK call completes

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of agent resources in the already-resolved plugin snapshot; toSdkCustomAgents reads each projected agent once and restricted agents add one boolean each to the existing customAgents array.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Agent files are read sequentially by the existing for loop. The whole projection runs concurrently with BYOK resolution and shell-tool creation; the diff does not change either level of concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The converter has no own cache and rereads each agent file on every non-ephemeral launch; warm behavior may benefit from the file service or OS cache. This behavior, cache keying, and absence of coalescing are unchanged. Ephemeral sessions continue to skip these reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete changed hunk and launcher call path establish unchanged I/O/concurrency and only O(1) local work per agent plus O(R) small payload growth.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin-agent counts and SDK serialization implementation vary, but the added payload is exactly one boolean property for each restricted agent and no extra call or read.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new local computation is constant-time per existing item, introduces no boundary call, and the bounded payload increase is not a meaningful performance mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run a chat turn where a selected plugin agent may delegate through the task tool
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After session setup, the runtime uses the projected custom-agent catalog to decide which siblings are model-invocable. A normal sibling still follows the existing task-tool and model path; a restricted sibling is now rejected before delegated model work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transitive from the task-tool delegation configured by src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotPluginConverters.ts:160
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the model for the parent turn and, when allowed, delegated subagent execution
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing model work per chat turn plus delegated work only for an allowed sibling; restricted siblings no longer proceed to delegated execution
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The missing runtime restriction could allow a restricted sibling onto the existing delegated model path; this diff adds no new model or network call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Allowed delegation remains on the turn critical path; for restricted siblings the diff prevents rather than adds downstream model work

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The catalog scales with plugin-agent count, while an individual tested delegation targets one sibling. Restricted entries are filtered by the runtime flag rather than triggering extra per-entry work on each turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The reviewed integration path issues two turns sequentially. Production task/model concurrency is runtime-owned and unchanged; the new flag only removes restricted agents from delegation eligibility.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The custom-agent catalog is established in session configuration and reused by the runtime for turns. No new lookup cache, miss retry, invalidation, or retained collection is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added disableModelInvocation field is consumed as a catalog restriction, and the integration change demonstrates allowed delegation succeeds while restricted delegation does not.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual model latency and how often agents attempt restricted delegation vary, but that uncertainty only affects the benefit of preventing the call, not the absence of a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The change can avoid unintended delegated model work and does not increase turn-time boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Synchronize and publish plugin customizations before launching a session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Active-client plugin synchronization parses plugin directories and publishes child customizations before snapshots feed session launch. The changed converter module is already reached from the Copilot agent, which already imports pluginParsers at runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse plugin manifests, directories, and agent files into the active snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing parsing per synchronized plugin and discovered resource
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Copilot agent and discovery code already imported and invoked pluginParsers; the new converter value import does not introduce plugin scanning or file reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronization must resolve before the updated plugin snapshot is published and used for launch

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish active-client customization state and receive session actions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing state publication per customization update
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same customization state crossed the same protocol boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the client-visible synchronized catalog, but the new boolean resolver does not add messages

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with plugin directories and their resources, as before; resolving the new flag during later SDK projection is constant-time per agent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Plugin parsing concurrency and synchronization sequencing are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved plugin snapshots are reused for catalog metadata, while the later agent prompt projection still rereads files as before. No cache state or lifecycle changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: imports and call sites show pluginParsers was already a runtime dependency of the owning Copilot agent and the diff adds no top-level I/O or eager initialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact plugin resource counts vary; no changed operation scales beyond the existing one boolean computation per projected agent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No eager-load or boundary-fanout regression. The runtime import reuses an already-loaded dependency on the owning product path and the helper has no side effects.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced session launch, plugin synchronization, SDK configuration transport, and delegated-agent execution. No high-confidence, diff-introduced performance issue was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
